stories.title: Accordion icons: the caret is the safest choice, and a plain link should just be underlined
stories.blurb: Vitaly Friedman sums up research on expand and collapse icons. Custom icons often fail to signal that an accordion will open, people tap icon and label about equally, and split menus where icon and label trigger different actions do harm. His rule of thumb: if it is a link, underline it and add no arrow or caret; where something expands, the caret is the most reliable icon.

stories.title: Yard NYC tells women to "send nudes", to themselves, as a monthly record for spotting breast changes
stories.blurb: For Breast Cancer Awareness Month the agency borrows a loaded online phrase and turns it into self-monitoring: regular photos let women notice changes over time. The campaign cites rising breast cancer rates among women under 50 and the fact that 85% of those diagnosed have no family history. For CEO Ruth Bernstein it is personal, she had early breast cancer herself.

stories.title: Accused of AI, Olivia Rodrigo's team showed the hand-made process instead of denying it
stories.blurb: After viewers declared a short animated sequence in the "Expectations" remix video to be generative AI, the official fan account posted a behind-the-scenes clip: character sketches, 2D and 3D animation, files played on a Windows Vista PC and filmed with a high-res camera to get the lo-fi look. Creative Bloq's argument is that showing the work ends the rumour where a formal denial would have fed it. Rolling Stone credits designer Jack Harrison with the analogue treatment.

stories.title: Getty Images files for bankruptcy and goes private through a Koch deal
stories.blurb: Design Week reports that Getty has formally filed, and frames the company as staying in business thanks to the Koch deal; it points to Reuters and the Wall Street Journal for the legal detail. Only the intro of the piece could be read, so what this means for licensing and contributors is not covered here.
